info.title: CodivUpload API Reference
info.description:
Publish content to 11 social media platforms with a single API call.

## Authentication

All API requests require a Bearer token in the `Authorization` header:

```
Authorization: Bearer YOUR_API_KEY
```

### Getting your API Key

1. Log in to [CodivUpload Dashboard](https://app.codivupload.com)
2. Go to **API Keys** from the sidebar menu
3. Click **Create API Key** and copy the key
4. Use the key in the `Authorization` header as shown above

> **Important:** API keys are shown only once at creation. Store them securely. If lost, revoke and create a new one.

> **Plan requirement:** API key access requires **Starter plan** or above. Free plan users can only use the dashboard UI.

### Quick Test

```bash
curl -X GET https://api.codivupload.com/v1/agency/profiles \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer YOUR_API_KEY"
```

A successful response returns your profiles:

```json
{
  "success": true,
  "profiles": [
    {
      "id": "550e8400-...",
      "profile_name": "my_brand",
      "social_accounts": { "youtube": true, "instagram": true, "tiktok": false }
    }
  ]
}
```

### Error Responses

| Status | Meaning | Example |
|---|---|---|
| `401` | Missing or invalid API key | `{ "error": "Missing or invalid Authorization header" }` |
| `403` | Plan tier insufficient — API keys require Starter plan or above | `{ "error": "This feature requires the Starter plan or above.", "required_tier": "starter", "current_tier": "free", "upgrade_url": "/dashboard/subscription" }` |

**Authorization rules:**
- All workspace members (owner and members) can list all profiles in their workspace.
- Use the `created_by` field to identify which user created each profile.

post.description:
Creates a new media management profile in the workspace.

**Authorization rules:**
- **Owner**: Can create profiles freely within the workspace.
- **Member**: Can create profiles — the profile is automatically linked to the creator.
- Members can only update/delete profiles they created. Owners can manage all profiles.

The `created_by` field is set automatically from the authenticated user.

Permanently deletes a profile and all its associated media assets via cascading deletion.

**Authorization rules:**
- **Owner**: Can delete any profile in the workspace.
- **Member**: Can only delete profiles they created (`created_by` must match the authenticated user).

post.description:
Publish content to multiple social media platforms with a single API call.

Use the `post_type` field to select the content type: **text**, **image**, **video**, or **document**. Each type shows the available fields and which platforms support it.

## Scheduling
- Omit `scheduled_date` to publish **immediately**.
- Provide a future date (ISO-8601 UTC) to **schedule** the post. The system automatically publishes it at the specified time. Max 365 days ahead.

## Platform Support

| Platform  | Text | Image | Video | Document |
|-----------|------|-------|-------|----------|
| X/Twitter | ✓    | ✓ (4) | ✓     | —        |
| YouTube   | —    | —     | ✓     | —        |
| Instagram | —    | ✓ (10)| ✓     | —        |
| Facebook  | ✓    | ✓     | ✓     | —        |
| LinkedIn  | ✓    | ✓ (9) | ✓     | ✓        |
| TikTok    | —    | ✓ (35)| ✓     | —        |
| Threads   | ✓    | ✓ (10)| ✓     | —        |
| Pinterest | —    | ✓ (1) | ✓     | —        |
| Google Business | ✓ | ✓ (1) | ✓  | —        |
| Bluesky   | ✓    | ✓ (4) | —     | —        |
| Snapchat  | —    | ✓ (1) | ✓     | —        |
| Telegram  | ✓    | ✓ (10)| ✓     | —        |
| Discord   | ✓    | ✓ (10)| ✓     | —        |
| Slack     | ✓    | ✓ (5) | ✓     | —        |
| WordPress | ✓    | ✓ (1, featured) | —  | —        |

*(Numbers in parentheses = max images per post)*

## Common Parameters (All Post Types)

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `post_type` | enum | Yes | `text`, `image`, `video`, or `document` |
| `profile_name` | string | Yes | Target profile name in your workspace |
| `platforms` | string[] | Yes | Target platforms to publish to |
| `media_urls` | string[] | Conditional | Public URLs of media files (from CDN Upload or external). Required for image/video/document. Use `/v1/upload-media` to upload files first. |
| `title` | string | No | Post title / video title / pin title |
| `description` | string | Conditional | Post caption / body text. Required for text posts. |
| `scheduled_date` | datetime | No | ISO-8601 UTC. Omit for immediate publishing. Cannot be used with `add_to_queue`. |
| `add_to_queue` | boolean | No | Auto-schedule to next available queue slot. **Requires Starter plan.** Configure slots in Settings → Queue. Cannot be used with `scheduled_date`. |
| `schedule_best_time` | boolean | No | Auto-schedule to the best posting time based on your last 90 days of analytics data. The system finds the optimal hour and day of week with highest engagement, then schedules the post for the next occurrence. Cannot be used with `scheduled_date` or `add_to_queue`. |
| `first_comment` | string | No | Auto-posted comment after publishing (Instagram, YouTube) |
| `auto_truncate` | boolean | No | Trim media arrays exceeding platform limits (default: false) |

## Platform-Specific Parameters

Each post type schema includes platform-specific override fields. These are only applied when the corresponding platform is in your `platforms` array.

Telegram authentication is bot-token based (not OAuth). Each connected social account stores one bot token and one chat ID (channel `@username` or numeric supergroup ID). The bot must be an admin of the target channel/group with permission to post.

### Discord (text, image & video)

| Parameter | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `discord_text` | string | shared `description` | Override message text. Max 2,000 chars. |
| `discord_media_urls` | url[] | — | **Override media** for Discord. Up to 10 images render as embeds; videos auto-unfurl inline. |

Discord authentication is webhook-based (not OAuth). Each connected social account stores one webhook URL (treated like a password and encrypted at rest). The webhook is created in the target channel's Integrations settings — anyone holding the URL can post.

### Slack (text, image & video)

| Parameter | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `slack_text` | string | shared `description` | Override message text. Max 40,000 chars. Slack mrkdwn rendered (`*bold*`, `_italic_`, `` `code` ``). |

## Per-Platform Media Override

By default, all platforms receive the same `media_urls`. To send **different media to specific platforms**, use per-platform media override fields:

| Parameter | Post Types | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `youtube_media_urls` | video | Override media for YouTube only |
| `instagram_media_urls` | image, video | Override media for Instagram only |
| `tiktok_media_urls` | image, video | Override media for TikTok only |
| `facebook_media_urls` | image, video | Override media for Facebook only |
| `pinterest_media_urls` | image, video | Override media for Pinterest only |
| `gbp_media_urls` | image, video | Override media for Google Business only |
| `snapchat_media_urls` | image, video | Override media for Snapchat only |
| `telegram_media_urls` | image, video | Override media for Telegram only (up to 10 as album) |
| `discord_media_urls` | image, video | Override media for Discord only (up to 10 image embeds) |
| `slack_media_urls` | image, video | Override media for Slack only (up to 5 image blocks) |
| `wordpress_media_urls` | text, image | Override featured image for WordPress (first item used as post cover) |

When a `{platform}_media_urls` is provided, it replaces `media_urls` for that specific platform. Other platforms continue using the shared `media_urls`.

**Example:** Post the same text but different video to YouTube and TikTok:
```json
{
  "post_type": "video",
  "media_urls": ["https://cdn.codivupload.com/.../horizontal.mp4"],
  "youtube_media_urls": ["https://cdn.codivupload.com/.../horizontal.mp4"],
  "tiktok_media_urls": ["https://cdn.codivupload.com/.../vertical.mp4"],
  "platforms": ["youtube", "tiktok"]
}
```

## Auto-Truncate
Set `auto_truncate: true` to automatically trim media arrays when they exceed a platform's limit (e.g., sending 8 images when X allows only 4). If false, the request returns a 400 error.

Limits are enforced per connected social account (not per user) within a 24-hour rolling window.

| Platform | Daily Limit (per account) |
|---|---|
| Instagram | 50 |
| TikTok | 15 |
| LinkedIn | 150 |
| YouTube | 10 |
| Facebook | 25 |
| X (Twitter) | 50 |
| Threads | 50 |
| Pinterest | 20 |
| Bluesky | 50 |

| Slack | 1,000 (1 req/sec sustained per webhook) |

When a daily limit is reached, the API returns a `429` error with details:
```json
{
  "success": false,
  "error": "Post verification failed",
  "violations": [{
    "platform": "instagram",
    "type": "hard_cap",
    "message": "Daily cap reached for instagram: 50/50 in last 24h",
    "used_last_24h": 50,
    "cap": 50
  }]
}
```

## Rate Limits
If a platform temporarily blocks publishing (rate limit), the post is automatically retried within a few minutes. You don't need to resend the request.

## Queue System (Starter plan and above)

Instead of specifying a `scheduled_date`, you can use `add_to_queue: true` to auto-schedule to the next available time slot.
Queue endpoints require **Starter plan or above**. Free plan users receive a `403` response with `required_tier: "starter"`.

- Configure slots (e.g., 9:00, 12:00, 17:00) via `POST /api/v1/queue/settings`
- Preview upcoming slots: `GET /api/v1/queue/preview?profile_name=xxx`
- Find next slot: `GET /api/v1/queue/next-slot?profile_name=xxx`
- Default slots: 9:00 AM, 12:00 PM, 5:00 PM UTC, every day, 1 post per slot

## YouTube API Quota

Each YouTube API operation consumes quota units from the project (10,000 units/day default):

| Operation | Unit Cost |
|---|---|
| Video upload (`videos.insert`) | 100 |
| Custom thumbnail (`thumbnails.set`) | 50 |
| Country restrictions (`videos.update`) | 50 |
| First comment (`commentThreads.insert`) | 50 |
| Caption/subtitle upload (`captions.insert`) | 400 |

Typical video upload with thumbnail = 150 units ≈ 66 videos/day.
Users can provide their own Google Cloud credentials for a dedicated 10,000 unit quota.

## Content Validation

Posts are validated before publishing:
- **Character limits** — enforced per platform (returns 400 if exceeded, unless `auto_truncate: true`)
- **Banned hashtags** — Instagram/Threads/Facebook posts are checked against a list of hashtags known to cause shadow bans. Returns 400 with `violations` array.
- **Duplicate content** — Similar content posted within 48 hours triggers a warning (non-blocking).
- **Media format** — Unsupported file formats are rejected at upload time.

## Usage Examples

> **Tip:** Use the **Example** dropdown in the request panel to load ready-to-use templates for each platform. Each example shows only the fields relevant to that scenario.

### Simple text post
```json
{
  "post_type": "text",
  "profile_name": "my_brand",
  "platforms": ["x", "threads", "bluesky"],
  "description": "Exciting news! Our new feature is live. Check it out!"
}
```

### YouTube video (common fields only — defaults handle the rest)
```json
{
  "post_type": "video",
  "profile_name": "my_brand",
  "platforms": ["youtube"],
  "media_urls": ["https://cdn.codivupload.com/.../video.mp4"],
  "title": "Product Launch 2026",
  "description": "Full walkthrough of our new features.",
  "youtube_privacy_status": "public",
  "youtube_tags": ["product", "launch", "tech"],
  "youtube_thumbnail_url": "https://cdn.codivupload.com/.../thumb.jpg",
  "youtube_category_id": "28"
}
```
*Other YouTube fields like `youtube_license`, `youtube_embeddable`, `youtube_default_language` etc. use sensible defaults. Add them only when you need to override.*

### Multi-platform video with per-platform media override
```json
{
  "post_type": "video",
  "profile_name": "my_brand",
  "platforms": ["youtube", "tiktok", "instagram"],
  "media_urls": ["https://cdn.codivupload.com/.../horizontal.mp4"],
  "tiktok_media_urls": ["https://cdn.codivupload.com/.../vertical.mp4"],
  "instagram_media_urls": ["https://cdn.codivupload.com/.../square.mp4"],
  "title": "Day in my life",
  "description": "Follow along for a day at the office!",
  "youtube_privacy_status": "public",
  "youtube_tags": ["vlog", "day-in-my-life"],
  "tiktok_privacy_level": "PUBLIC_TO_EVERYONE",
  "tiktok_post_mode": "DIRECT_POST",
  "instagram_media_type": "REELS",
  "instagram_share_to_feed": true
}
```
*YouTube receives `media_urls` (horizontal). TikTok receives `tiktok_media_urls` (vertical). Instagram receives `instagram_media_urls` (square). Each platform also gets its own override fields — fields for other platforms are ignored.*

### TikTok draft mode (send to inbox)
```json
{
  "post_type": "video",
  "profile_name": "my_brand",
  "platforms": ["tiktok"],
  "media_urls": ["https://cdn.codivupload.com/.../clip.mp4"],
  "tiktok_post_mode": "MEDIA_UPLOAD"
}
```
*In MEDIA_UPLOAD mode, no metadata (title, privacy, interactions) is sent. Add details in the TikTok app before publishing.*

### Scheduled post
```json
{
  "post_type": "text",
  "profile_name": "my_brand",
  "platforms": ["linkedin", "x"],
  "description": "We are hiring! Senior engineers wanted. DM us.",
  "scheduled_date": "2026-04-15T09:00:00Z",
  "linkedin_visibility": "PUBLIC",
  "x_reply_settings": "following"
}
```

post.description:
Upload a file to the CodivUpload CDN (Cloudflare R2). Returns a public URL that can be used in the `media_urls` field when creating a post.

## Two Upload Methods

### 1. File Upload (multipart/form-data)
Send the file directly as form data. Best for UI file pickers and drag-drop uploads.

```
curl -X POST /v1/upload-media \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer YOUR_TOKEN" \
  -F "file=@photo.jpg" \
  -F "profile_name=WhiskeyBlues"
```

### 2. URL Upload (application/json)
Provide a public URL and we fetch + store it on CDN. Best for external integrations.

```json
{
  "url": "https://example.com/image.jpg",
  "profile_name": "WhiskeyBlues",
  "type": "image"
}
```

## Parameters

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `file` | binary | Yes* | File to upload (multipart mode) |
| `url` | string | Yes* | Public URL to fetch (JSON mode) |
| `profile_name` | string | Yes | Target profile name in your workspace |
| `type` | string | No | Force file type: image, video, document. Auto-detected if omitted. |

*One of `file` or `url` is required.

## Supported Formats
- **Images:** JPG, PNG, WebP, GIF, BMP
- **Videos:** MP4, MOV, WebM, AVI, MKV
- **Documents:** PDF, DOC, DOCX, PPT, PPTX

## Limits
- Max file size depends on your plan
- Large files (>64 MB) are automatically uploaded in parallel chunks for reliability
- URL fetch timeout: 2 minutes

## CDN Storage
- Files are stored on the CodivUpload CDN (Cloudflare R2)
- Path: `{workspace}/{profile}/{upload_id}/original.{ext}`
- Files expire after 30 days if not linked to a post
- After post is published, files remain for 30 days (platforms copy the media)

post.description:
Create a new webhook endpoint. Maximum 5 endpoints per workspace.

A signing secret (`whsec_...`) is returned **only once** in the creation response. Store it securely — it is used to verify webhook signatures.

## Supported Events

| Event | Trigger |
|---|---|
| `post.success` | A post was successfully published to a platform |
| `post.failed` | A post failed to publish to a platform |
| `post.scheduled` | A post was created with a future `scheduled_date` |
| `post.deleted` | A scheduled or draft post was deleted |
| `profile.connected` | A new social account was connected via OAuth |
| `profile.disconnected` | A social account connection was revoked |

## Webhook Delivery

When an event fires, CodivUpload sends a `POST` request to your URL with:

**Headers:**
| Header | Description |
|---|---|
| `Content-Type` | `application/json` |
| `X-Webhook-Event` | Event type (e.g. `post.success`) |
| `X-Webhook-Signature` | HMAC-SHA256 hex digest of the request body, signed with your secret |

**Body:**
```json
{
  "event": "post.success",
  "timestamp": "2026-04-08T14:30:00.000Z",
  "workspace_id": "ws_abc123",
  "data": {
    "post_id": "550e8400-...",
    "destination_id": "660e8400-...",
    "platform": "instagram",
    "post_url": "https://www.instagram.com/p/ABC123/"
  }
}
```

## Verifying Signatures

To verify that a webhook came from CodivUpload, compute the HMAC-SHA256 of the raw request body using your signing secret and compare it with the `X-Webhook-Signature` header:

```javascript
const crypto = require("crypto");

function verifyWebhook(body, signature, secret) {
  const expected = crypto
    .createHmac("sha256", secret)
    .update(body)
    .digest("hex");
  return crypto.timingSafeEqual(
    Buffer.from(signature),
    Buffer.from(expected)
  );
}
```

```python
import hmac, hashlib

def verify_webhook(body: bytes, signature: str, secret: str) -> bool:
    expected = hmac.new(secret.encode(), body, hashlib.sha256).hexdigest()
    return hmac.compare_digest(signature, expected)
```

## Delivery Behavior

- Timeout: 10 seconds per delivery attempt
- All deliveries are logged (success and failure)
- Webhooks are fire-and-forget — they do not block post publishing
- Failed deliveries do not automatically retry (check delivery logs in Dashboard)
